draft.title: The history of excavation
card: Digging at Herculaneum began in 1738 and at Pompeii in 1748, under the Bourbon rulers of Naples. The diggers wanted statues, paintings and other treasures for royal collections.
These early digs were poorly recorded. Finds were often taken away from where they lay, so the evidence of how a room or house was used was lost.
Giuseppe Fiorelli directed the dig at Pompeii from 1863. He recorded each building and dug layer by layer from the top down.
Fiorelli also began making plaster casts of bodies. Plaster was poured into hollows left in the ash by bodies that had rotted away. Excavation and conservation continue today.
draft.remember: Early digs sought treasure. Fiorelli's records turned digging into a study of how people lived.

a.q: Why did Fiorelli's methods give historians better evidence than the early digs?
opts: He recorded where finds lay, so their context was kept
He dug faster, so more of the town was uncovered
He collected more statues for the royal collections
He avoided the ash layers, so the finds stayed intact
a.why: Recording each building and digging layer by layer kept the setting of finds, which shows how places were used. Speed or more treasure would not do this, since the early diggers took finds from where they lay and lost that evidence.
a.clue: Think about what is lost when a find is removed without a record.

b.q: An archaeologist at Pompeii draws each room, notes where every object was found, and digs from the top layer down. Which earlier approach does this work most clearly reject?
opts: Removing finds for collections with little recording
Pouring plaster into hollows left by bodies
Continuing excavation after the eruption's anniversary
Studying houses as well as public buildings
b.why: Recording find spots and digging in layers is the opposite of the early treasure hunts, where finds were taken without records. Plaster casts were part of Fiorelli's careful approach, so they are not rejected.
b.clue: Which method did the early diggers use that careful recording replaced?

a.best: He recorded where finds lay, so their context was kept

b.best: Removing finds for collections with little recording

check.summary: No problems found. The dates (Herculaneum 1738, Pompeii 1748), the Bourbon treasure-hunting, Fiorelli from 1863 and his plaster casts all check out, and both questions have one clear answer.
